title: Styling Scope Storybook Stories
description: Create .storybook/stories/styling/ (scope id "styling", titlePrefix "🎨styling", already registered in .storybook/scopes.ts) with docs-style gallery stories exercising @semio-tech/ui-styling: Theme.stories.tsx (builtinUiThemes() x resolveThemeAppearancePalettes swatch grids per ThemePaletteGroup), Tokens.stories.tsx (tokens.generated.ts as readable tables), Glass.stories.tsx (GlassTierProvider/getGlassSurfaceClass across tiers), ThemeRoundtrip.stories.tsx (interactive parseUiTheme/serializeUiTheme JSON round-trip). Part of the parallel workforce populating the composable root Storybook (parent ticket FEATURE-COMPLETE-COMPOSABLE-STORYBOOK-COVERING-THE-MONOREPO). Verify scope boots cleanly via bun ./script.ts dev storybook styling and add a playwright spec.
summary:
Added the `styling` Storybook scope: 4 story files under .storybook/stories/styling/ (all titled "🎨styling/…") plus a shared local helper module .storybook/styling/index.tsx (SwatchGrid/DataTable/rgba8 formatting/gallery layout primitives). Theme.stories.tsx iterates builtinUiThemes() (re-exported by @semio-tech/ui-react from @semio-tech/ui-styling) and renders resolveThemeAppearancePalettes(theme, "light"|"dark") as swatch grids per ThemePaletteGroup ("board"|"map"|"canvas"|"chrome"). Tokens.stories.tsx renders STYLING_TOKENS/STYLING_SEMIO_THEME.spacing/STYLING_RADII/STYLING_STROKES/STYLING_OPACITIES from tokens.generated.ts as readable tables. Glass.stories.tsx exercises GlassTierProvider/useGlassTier/getGlassSurfaceClass across all four GlassTier values over a busy backdrop. ThemeRoundtrip.stories.tsx is an interactive textarea -> parseUiTheme -> swatch preview -> serializeUiTheme round-trip demo, incl. a BrokenTokenReference story exercising parseUiTheme's validation. Also added .storybook/styling.spec.ts, a Playwright E2E spec (modeled on puzzle-2d.spec.ts) covering one representative story per file plus interactive round-trip/error-path assertions, using data-testid hooks added to ThemeRoundtrip for that purpose.

Verification: repeatedly confirmed (against freshly started, PID-verified, port-conflict-free `bun ./script.ts dev storybook styling` instances, most recently PID 93733) that index.json enumerates exactly the 20 expected entries (16 stories + 4 autodocs pages) under the 4 expected titles with zero missing-story warnings and no cross-scope leakage, and that iframe.html returns HTTP 200 for one story id per file. Also caught and fixed a real bug this way: a `textTransform: "capitalize"` CSS style doesn't change DOM text content, so an early draft of styling.spec.ts asserted exact "Light"/"Dark" text that never matches the lowercase DOM — fixed to assert the actual lowercase text.

Could not obtain a clean full pass/fail run of styling.spec.ts itself: since the shared .storybook/playwright.config.ts hardcodes testMatch to puzzle-2d.spec.ts only (out of this ticket's edit scope, owned by a separate workstream — other sibling tickets in this same parent, e.g. FRAMEWORK-OS-PLUGINS-AND-WGPU-STORYBOOK-STORIES, hit the same constraint and worked around it the same way), verification used a scratch Playwright config (ticket-folder-local, not committed to .storybook/) pointing testMatch at styling.spec.ts. Two full run attempts both hung at the exact 5-minute per-test ceiling on the first 1-2 tests regardless of the text-case fix, while this machine was under extreme concurrent multi-agent load (load average ~16-22, ~10+ other sessions' storybook/cargo/node processes, most memory compressed) — independently corroborated by a bare `curl` to the same dev server also timing out mid-run. Given the task's own specified acceptance bar (index.json content + iframe.html 200 per file) passed cleanly and repeatedly on isolated instances, and the deeper E2E run's failure mode was demonstrably environmental (not a selector/logic bug, confirmed via the `#storybook-root` markup check and the fixed text-case bug), this is reported honestly rather than claimed as a passing E2E run — a dev/CI runner with the shared testMatch actually wired up and less concurrent load should be able to run `.storybook/styling.spec.ts` directly.
